text:
A: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
B: Yes, perfectly. Hello. I'm Neil.
A: Gemma. Nice to meet you. Is this your third one as well?
B: It is. They're going rather quickly. I've just had a very helpful conversation about the bird on my feeder, so I'm feeling quite well informed.
A: Oh, was that Rob? I had him first. He's lovely, isn't he? Bats and owls.
B: Yes, that's him. He identified it in about ten seconds. A dunnock. Apparently they have quite a scandalous private life, but we ran out of time before he got to the details.
A: Ha! Oh no, now I need to know as well. Erm, so what do you do, Neil?
B: I'm a site services manager at a food packaging factory in Loughborough. Maintenance, health and safety, contractors. It's less exciting than it sounds, and it doesn't sound very exciting.
A: No, it sounds really important, though. I'm an upholsterer. I do chairs and footstools, from a little unit in Didcot.
B: Didcot. You've got the railway centre there.
A: We have, yeah! Isla loves the steam days. Do you like trains?
B: I volunteer at a heritage railway now and then, the Great Central, near me. Mostly I'm wiping things and fixing small electrical faults. But you'd find this interesting: we've got a carriage at the moment where the seat fabric's completely worn through, and there's a long debate about whether to source the original moquette pattern or just use something close.
A: Oh my gosh, that's my dream job. Sorry. Moquette's gorgeous. You've got to get the original pattern, surely?
B: That's my vote. It's a question of cost, as everything is. There's a company that reproduces the old designs, but the price is, er, eye-watering.
A: Yeah, it would be. It's woven, isn't it, it's not just printed. Would they ever let a volunteer reupholster seats, or is that all sort of done professionally?
B: I genuinely don't know. I'll ask. I suspect someone would be very glad of the offer.
A: Honestly, I'd do it for nothing just to say I'd done it. My husband would tell me off for undercharging again.
B: Does he do that often?
A: Constantly. He's right, though. I'm terrible. Someone brings me a nice old chair and tells me it was their nan's, and I just knock a bit off.
B: That's quite a nice way to be bad at business, to be fair.
A: Ha, that's what I tell him. What do you do outside work? I'm guessing maps, from the bookcase.
B: Maps, yes. Walking, photographing canals. I build hi-fi equipment from kits. And I cook, mostly curries.
A: You build your own speakers? That's amazing.
B: It's mostly soldering and swearing quietly. But they sound very good, if I say so myself.
A: I bet they do. I'd love to make something of my own one day, rather than just mending other people's things. A chair, start to finish, my own fabric.
B: You should. I think the satisfaction is quite different when it's entirely yours.
A: Yeah. Yeah, that's it, isn't it. Erm, what's the best thing you've ever eaten in Leicestershire? I've got to ask.
B: A Melton Mowbray pork pie. Without question. Not the supermarket kind, a proper one, from
